# Swap the database with one deployment file (offline) - generated by build_tapes.py from clips.py; do not edit by hand
# SA lines only: render with digital-demand-factory/screen-demos/generate_two_voice.py

[intro]
SA: "This clip is about the configuration axis, recorded without the Region. A 28 September capture shows kind moving from PostgreSQL to DynamoDB Local, a development stand-in. An older capture compares the PostgreSQL adapter in both clusters. The claim is that the store choice lives in a deployment file and leaves application code unchanged."

[screen_01]
SA: "The persistence file names a backend and its options. This variant points at DynamoDB Local inside the cluster, with placeholder credentials. It exists only for this exercise."
SA: "In the composition root, a small registry maps each backend name to a builder. The composition root is the only module that reads the environment, and the only one that picks an adapter. A backend module loads only when it is selected, so the in-memory path needs no database driver."

[screen_02]
SA: "This dated terminal capture shows health before the kind deployment change, the persistence file diff, and health after the rollout. The new response names the DynamoDB repository against a local endpoint. The capture is from a completed rehearsal, not a live switch in this video."
SA: "The script also hashes the Python code before and after and prints identical hashes. DynamoDB Local had to be running first. Changing a variable does not create a database."

[screen_03]
SA: "This part is the capture from the twenty-sixth of September, taken while both clusters used PostgreSQL. The PostgreSQL adapter was hashed inside a running pod on each cluster, and in the checkout. All three matched. Aurora in the Region and CloudNativePG on the laptop ran the same adapter bytes."
SA: "What differs is where the connection settings and credentials come from: Secrets Manager and External Secrets in the Region, and a secret generated inside the cluster on premises."

[outro]
SA: "This does not move existing data. The two stores start separately, so a real cutover still needs a migration plan and a switch. And it only works because a PostgreSQL adapter already exists. Moving to a different data model needs new adapter code, which is the next clip."
SA: "The takeaway: once the adapter exists, choosing the store is a deployment decision."
